thresholdDerivation.whyThisKeyExists: lhci parses lighthouserc.json with JSON.parse (node_modules/@lhci/utils/src/lighthouserc.js), so the file cannot hold a comment. flattenRcToConfig reads only ci, lhci, ci:client and ci:server, so this sibling key never reaches lhci. It is the derivation for the numbers under ci.assert.assertions, kept in the file a reader edits them in.
thresholdDerivation.population: 37 complete batches, 185 individual Lighthouse runs, read from the retained .lighthouseci artifacts of the 40 most recent Performance Budget runs (2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08). This supersedes the earlier derivation entirely: that one had to reconstruct total-blocking-time from CENSORED data, because lhci prints a metric's numeric value only for an assertion that FAILS, and it left largest-contentful-paint and resource-summary:script:size at n = 0. The artifacts now retain the full LHR for every run, pass or fail, so all three assertions are derived from exact observations.
thresholdDerivation.theColdStart: THE finding, and the reason the budget was flaky rather than wrong. Run 1 of a batch exceeded EVERY other run in that batch 32 times out of 37. Total-blocking-time: cold p50 2816.7 ms, cold max 12006 ms, against a warm p50 of 797.5 ms. That is the Next.js production server compiling the authenticated route on first request, not the page being slow. With numberOfRuns 5 and median aggregation, one huge outlier does not set the median but it does bias it upward by one order statistic, from between the 2nd and 3rd warm value to the 3rd. apps/web/perf/lhci-hermetic-auth.cjs now performs a warmup navigation before collection, which removes the artifact at its source rather than tolerating it in the threshold.
thresholdDerivation.total-blocking-time: 950 -> 1200 ms. The old 950 was derived against a population that INCLUDED the cold start and projected about 1.3 percent failures. Measured against the real distribution it sat at p90 of the batch medians and failed 4 of 37 runs, 10.8 percent, on three different branches, with the same branch both passing and failing. A gate that fails roughly one clean run in ten teaches everyone to re-run reds without reading them. Warm batch medians (n = 37): min 510.2, p50 795.8, p90 945.8, p95 961.7, p99 1036.0, max 1058.2; mean 792.1 with sd 131.4, so mean+3sd is 1186.3 and mean+4sd is 1317.7. 1200 sits just above mean+3sd and 13.4 percent above the largest median ever observed, and fails 0 of the 37 clean batches. It is not 'a gate that asserts nothing': the app's warm median is about 795 ms, so 1200 still fails any regression that adds roughly 400 ms of main-thread blocking, which is what this gate exists to catch. Re-derive if the warm median moves by more than about 20 percent.
thresholdDerivation.largest-contentful-paint: 7000 is UNCHANGED, and it is now DERIVED rather than a placeholder. The previous revision recorded n = 0 because every observation was missing. Warm batch medians (n = 37): min 3639.5, p50 4743.4, p90 5319.3, p95 5608.6, p99 5808.3, max 5854.1; mean 4655.2 with sd 656.4, so mean+3sd is 6624.5. 7000 is 19.6 percent above the largest median observed and sits between 3 and 4 standard deviations. It has never fired in 117 runs of this workflow, and that is now known to be correct headroom rather than an unmeasured guess.
thresholdDerivation.resource-summary:script:size: 820000 is UNCHANGED, and it is now DERIVED. Batch medians of script transferSize (n = 37): min 749508, p50 750481, p90 769798, p95 769913, p99 770137, max 770185 bytes. The natural spread is only 2.8 percent, far tighter than the timing metrics, because bundle size is deterministic where main-thread work is not. 820000 is 6.5 percent above the largest median observed, which is deliberately tight: a budget this stable should catch a real dependency or code-splitting regression rather than absorb one.
thresholdDerivation.aggregation: numberOfRuns 5 with aggregationMethod median. Neither may be lowered without re-deriving every threshold above. numberOfRuns is NOT raised to compensate for noise, because the warmup removes the dominant source of it: with run 1 warm, the median is taken over 5 comparable runs instead of 4 plus an outlier, which is already a more stable estimator than adding runs to a contaminated sample would be.
